item.title: New workshop: Postcards (Christmas or not) in cyanotype.
item.description: Prussian blue is one of the oldest pigments in photography and also the cheapest to make: two iron salts, water and light. In 1842, John Herschel mixed ferric ammonium citrate and potassium ferricyanide and found that where ultraviolet light fell the paper turned blue, while the rest washed away in water. No silver, no darkroom and no developer: an exposure and a tray. Herschel wanted a way to copy notes and drawings, and for decades the process was used for the engineering plans that are still called blueprints.
